Subject: Confidentiality & announcement rights — Lodestar Order Form

Hi Avery,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we progress on the order form we wanted to loop in legal around a couple of publicity points that came up in our procurement review. Two asks from our side: 1) Lodestar needs a short window to approve any marketing quote that uses our name (we've flagged 7 business days in past contracts), and 2) we prefer logo use to be limited to a non-prominent placement on customer lists (no co-branded press release without explicit approval).

I understand Redwood typically includes a standard publicity clause in the MSA/order form. Could you share the exact language you're proposing and confirm whether you can add a narrow approval window and an embargo carveout for product announcements? Kevin from our legal team is CC'd — he'll follow up with specific redlines if needed.

Attached: Lodestar_OrderForm_Redline_v3.docx (we've highlighted the sections)

Appreciate it — would like to keep this moving so we can hit our onboarding target in January.

Best,
Tamara Singh
Chief Partnerships Officer
Lodestar Health

Date: Wed, 4 Dec 2024 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Confidentiality & announcement rights — Lodestar Order Form

Tamara — thanks for the clear summary and for sending the marked-up order form. Looping in Laura (sales ops) for the order form flow and Mina (legal) for the clause language. Marissa from marketing is on CC to help expedite approvals should we agree on a short testimonial/quote.

Quick note on Redwood's defaults: our standard MSA includes a publicity paragraph that allows the vendor to list the customer on a public 'customers' page and request a short quote for case studies. We usually include a 10-business-day approval window for quotations. We can narrow that to 7 business days as a concession, and we can add an explicit embargo carveout (e.g., customer may request an embargo until an agreed date or until regulatory signoff).

Mina — can you propose language that: 1) permits logo listing on a customer page, 2) permits a one-sentence quote with 7 business days to approve, and 3) requires a separate written approval for press releases/co-branded announcements? Please keep the language tight so procurement/finance can accept it without a long loop.

Tamara — if you prefer, Kevin can send his redlines and Mina will compare and propose a final amendment text we can attach to the order form.

Thanks,
Avery Johnson
Enterprise Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
To: avery.johnson@redwood.com, tamara.singh@lodestar.ai
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 4 Dec 2024 11:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Confidentiality & announcement rights — Lodestar Order Form

Hi all — here is concise proposed wording that should address Lodestar's ask while keeping Redwood's ability to use customer references for standard marketing. Suggest adding this as an Annex to the order form ("Publicity Annex") rather than changing the MSA body.

--- Proposed Publicity Annex (suggested, plain text) ---
1) Customer Listing: Customer grants Redwood the non-exclusive right to display Customer's name and logo on Redwood's public customer list and website.
2) Quotes and Testimonials: Redwood may request a short quote (no more than one sentence). Customer will approve or reasonably decline the quote within 7 business days of receipt. Failure to respond within 7 business days constitutes approval.
3) Press Releases & Co-branded Announcements: Any press release or co-branded announcement referencing Customer requires explicit prior written approval signed by an authorized representative of Customer. Approval shall not be unreasonably withheld.
4) Embargo: Customer may request an embargo for a specified date; Redwood will not publicly disclose Customer's participation prior to the agreed embargo date.
--- end ---

A few operational notes: 1) I added a reasonable default for failure to respond (auto-approval) to avoid indefinite holds; if Lodestar absolutely cannot accept auto-approval, we can remove that provision and set a manual fallback. 2) Marissa, recommend we capture the internal review SLA for marketing approvals (we typically can turn approvals within 48 hours on our side).

Tamara / Kevin — happy to take direct redlines against this text. If acceptable, we can attach it as Annex A to the order form and sign off as part of the procurement packet.

Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Kevin Wong <kevin.wong@lodestar.ai>

Mina — thanks for the quick draft. A couple of proposed edits from Lodestar legal attached as a tracked redline (see Lodestar_OrderForm_Redline_v3.docx). High-level comments: 1) we cannot accept auto-approval by silence (we'll change the failure-to-respond language to require affirmative approval or escalation to a named executive after 14 business days), and 2) we need to exclude any use of our logo on promotional materials other than a customer list (no product screenshots or co-branding).

If Redwood insists on an auto-approval timeframe, suggest 14 business days instead of 7. We also request a clause that requires Redwood to route any proposed public quote through a dedicated marketing contact (we've listed Tamara as that contact).

Attached: Lodestar_OrderForm_Redline_v3.docx (redlines)

Let us know if you'd prefer a short call to get to final text.

Best,
Kevin Wong
Head of Legal Operations
Lodestar Health

I'll attach the reconciled annex once Mina and Kevin confirm the final wording. For procurement: Laura, please hold the order form (HS-123456) for signature pending annex approval; Tamara please confirm if your procurement timeline still targets the January onboarding window.
